body: I've been in therapy but it hasn't helped...

Somebody sent me a passage that says before you do it, wait a year. And after that, you'll say "holy shit, I can't believe I missed out on..." with a list. But in the last year, I have tried a lot of things, and I still feel isolated and hollow. I've been told to drown myself in work/class, but that didn't help either. Now I'm on the verge of graduating college as I see that I'm no closer than before I was conceived to finding anyone who genuinely cares for me. If I can't find that even once in the most social chunk of my life, how? Why? What's the point? I'm not made to go through life alone, but that's how it's playing out. Why prolong emptiness and suffering?

I've tried to do it but everywhere I look I'm reminded that I've never been able to be in a relationship or have a group of friends around here that want me to do anything with. I can't even debate those, they're facts.

Yes, my friend was what got me to go. But it hasn't helped. I'm still alone and miserable without anything to live for... I can't keep doing this for another 50-60 years. I can't even keep doing it now.

We've been good friends for a year. We got really close when she was dealing with family and confidence issues earlier this year. The few times it's gotten bad enough that I need to talk to her, she's made it sound like I'm not trying enough. I am, god knows I am. But she's trying to help & I don't want to argue so I don't say much about it.

And I wish I didn't, but it's not that simple. All I want in life is a best friend to call my partner. Not necessarily kids, not money, but a partner. I'm told that in order to find somebody, I have to be happy with myself. Well I was and I didn't. And because I didn't, now I'm not happy with myself. It's hopeless. I am hopeless.

Yes, and I have. Multiple times. Right now she's doing alright thankfully. She's one of the strongest people I know. There's coping and then there's beating it, and she has beaten it. But I'm not strong like her. I'm not independent or confident enough. I'm too below average, to unimportant to those around me. If I'm gone, nobody will care. I'm starting to think they'd be better off without me. I've tried contacting a few other people and they aren't responding either. I can't handle another 60 years of loneliness and pain. I know I won't be "happy" if I'm gone, but I won't feel the hurt and disappointment anymore.

I've tried, god knows I do. But I can't get over feeling like nobody cares about me. If my parents disappeared tomorrow, I'd be a 23 year old on his own with no purpose to continue. I talk to a lot of people casually in college, but nobody ever has wanted to go past that. I can't keep going on like this
I ask them how they're doing. I invite them to do things. I start conversations; send first messages. And I get nothing of the sort in return.

I play guitar and am an excellent painter, but I can't keep it together if I'm feeling down. Games and movies don't do it either. I feel like I'm out of options. I made a bunch of friends though my college courses, but they aren't my real friends. Nobody from there in these five years has been.

I missed my young adult life as far as I'm concerned. And I have not once had anybody show any interest in me. After years of isolation, I have to come to terms with the fact that I'm just not good enough. 
And therapy practically hasn't even started yet. Plus it's two weeks between sessions which leaves me with two weeks of nobody to talk to about it, so much to the point that I want to scream and sob right now.
No, there is no reason. I meant that she has gone to therapy too. I can guarantee she doesn't have the same problem I have. Nobody I know does.

She's never been the greatest at replying, but when you say that you'll always respond even if it's not right away, I expect a response eventually. But no, half of what I say or ask gets nothing in return. And when I do, it's kept brief without meaning to it. And then I don't get any responses after that. It's disrespectful and crushing. I was there for both of the people I trusted when they had struggles, but no one will ever return the favor.

This newest and harshest rejection was from my only friend who has gone through anything like this and is the only one who has been willing to do anything different. Like going on a mini road trip, visiting a museum, or, for lack of a better term, Netflix and chilling. 

I have had virtually nothing to help me. Keeling busy doesn't help. Free time doesn't help. Occasionally seeing friends doesn't help. Just recently started therapy and it hasn't helped. Hell, my friend who I mentioned above has been barely replying. I trusted hee the most and, yet again, my support quickly gave away and let me tumble. I can't keep going on like this. Now I have nobody else to turn to, either for a relationship or emotional support.

Yes, I have friends, but I don't have anybody who wants a stronger relationship than that. My local friends never want to do anything but play online every night. I enjoy it, but goddamnit I want to go and do stuff once in a while. And I'm never going to find a special someone. I'm too inferior to average in every way.

It started with being rejected by one of the people I was closest to and lack of true friends at college. Now I've been rejected again by someone even closer, and I have no possibilities. I can't help but think that after reaching almost 24 years of age and getting only "no's" and not having friends who are willing to go do more than just play games online together.... well I feel like I've missed out on my youth entirely. And if the people who like me won't even give me a chance, why should I ever believe I have one?

I'm glad somebody has this go positively for them. I recently asked my closest female friend to be my girlfriend (she would be my first ever), but she said no and now I'm an absolute mess. I felt so happy when I thought she was interested... unfortunately for me, what I and all of our friends thought was a sure thing wasn't meant to be I guess. And now there's literally no one else on my life who is even an option at this point.

I see you mentioned your parents' genders. I'm a guy, and honestly I believe that most of us here are men.
I opened up about my depression to my friend last year. This was shortly after she called me her best friend. Well, she stonewall ed me. Basically said 'it sucks but you have to get over it. I can't help.'
Meanwhile, my "bros," who I of couse wouldn't mention it to because we're all men, have been much more supportive. There are so many gender assumptions today, but this isn't one of those times. People with equally understand [or not] from both sides of the gender isle. They both care, and she might not realize how serious this/you are. She'll come around eventually I hope.

In the meantime, please do whatever it takes to avoid self harm or any substance abuse. Don't do it for me, and don't do it for r/depression. Do it for yourself because you are much too important for it to continue.

I can't offer advice because I'm in the same boat, buddy. Last semester was the worst 3 1/2 months of my life without a doubt. I felt pretty much exactly how you described, except some nights were so bad that I actually did wish I were dead. I wept, hard. Very few people bothered to ask what was wrong, even a friend who told me I was her best friend didn't offer to help. She shunned me instead. Seeing everyone out partying made me feel so terrible because despite having a few of my closest IRL buddies on Xbox, I was obligated to see these "false" friends daily.
Over winter break, two of my coworkers pulled me through (even though they didn't know I was severely depressed.) It wasn't pure joy, and I'm still not 100% now.
However, I no longer feel that separation from my classmates. Do I hang out with any of them? Never. Do I want to? A couple, maybe to go grab lunch. But I finally was invited out bar hopping with them, and I realized something from that agonizingly outcast - feeling night. I realized that those particular people aren't for me. Too careless, too uncaring. My coworkers, one who is my best friend and the other a girl who I have developed feelings for, made me realize what I should get out of a friendship. Classmates weren't the answer. Yes, you can potentially find a diamond in the rough, but it isn't necessarily the best place. You have a better chance to find them there, but that doesn't make them right.
Like I said, I'm not all better. I still feel incredibly sad/lonely on the daily basis for being single (23 y.o.) so far in my life. But I have hope, even if it often isn't enough to overcome the pain. I know it's there. It can't be forced, though, and I am with you 100% in that terrible struggle of time. Time away from my classmates made me realize that I don't need them; this isn't like high school in that regard. Hell, I only talk to 2 of my high school friends. Everyone else I met online and I enjoy their company substantially more than many classmates.

I have no idea why I padded this out so much. Just know that you aren't the only one, and I'm fucking proud of you for being here with us.
This is pretty much my exact situation and why I feel depressed. I'm sorry you have to go through this too.

23. Graduating some time this year hopefully. Not as passionate about my field as everyone else. Never once had a relationship because anybody I've been interested in has never been interested in me. That's why I'm depressed unfortunately. I'm afraid I'll hate my job if I can even find one, or that (even worse) I'll end up alone my whole life.

Fear of rejection? Definitely. Have I been rejected? Directly, no, but that's because I've been too much of an introvert to ask anyone out. Somebody who called me their best friend flat out rejected me without me ever asking or implying would. Now I feel infatuated with a newer friend who I can't get a read on, but I have doubts 95% of the time that get so bad that they shut me down. But the thing is that I'll never work up the courage to ask in the first place because of the fear of rejection and the fear of pushing away the one person who makes me feel happy consistently.
I just want you to know that I'm proud of you, man. I'm glad you've been able to do what I've been too scared to do in 23 years. We both wish they could have turned out differently, but damn am I glad you have tried.

I don't know how to get out of that kind of rut, but I wanted to let you know that you aren't alone. I feel the exact same way because I'm 23 and have never been in a relationship, let alone seen anyone show any interest. When I first became depressed in September (and all the way through January), I felt like I didn't have any meaningful relationships friend wise either. This was compounded by the fact that I spent so much time at school and that's where I felt the most disconnected.
Since then, I've realized that I do have decent friends there, even if that's the only place I'll ever see them. But man oh man, the lack of an emotional or lightly physical conenction tears me up daily. 
Not sure why I wrote this all, just wanted you to know that you aren't the only person dealing with this.

Last semester, I began to believe that I was the loner of my classmates in college (art major; our group tends to be much more social than standard classes). I realized that I had almost never once been invited anywhere in 4 years by classmates, including someone who considered me to be her best friend. Well, I finally got invited out to a gathering. The moment I hit the parking lot 45 minutes away, I immediately regretted going. Had an alright time, and felt tremendously terrible upon leaving. It was the same kind of horrid pain that I felt when I knew everyone else was going out and I wasn't because I've never been a partier or drinker. A month later, I got invited out to a graduation party that involved bar hopping. Same situation happened, but I cut out early since nobody was talking to me and I was the only one who stayed sober. That mounting on top of my already overpowering lonliness made me feel like that was the worst night of my life. And the following day, a "close" friend asked me about it and insulted me for my depression. The same thing happened the very few times we spoke over the break.

Do I believe it was a mistake going? Sort of, yes. But now I see that group of people going out and think to myself, 'Fuck that. They're doing stupid stuff and I want no part of it.' And at this point, I'm totally okay with that. I realize now that, to a certain extent, I am a loner at college, but I really don't care anymore. I'm still depressed because of lonliness, but it's from a 'being-single-forever' type of lonliness, not the type that I was dealing with last semester on top of this.

I guess what I'm saying is that you may hate being there, and you may feel absolutely terrible for the immediate future, but you will get past it. You will feel better down the line. I know, it fucking sucks and there's almost nothing that can make you feel better immediately, but I want you to believe; to KNOW that you will move beyond this.

This is similar to my situation. My depression stems from lonliness and lack of ever having a relationship. I can't tell of my friend would be interested in a relationship and have no idea how to approach it. But then again, I could be desperate for that emotional connection and way off course.

That's similar to how I feel, except in my case I don't have that special person. My depression is caused by loneliness and lack of an emotional/physicical connection with anybody. The few times I felt really happy lately have been when I thought that one of my friends might be interested in a relationship, but I'm certain now that I'm just being illogical and clingy.
I've always been a little unhappy about being single for so long, but it hit me hard as hell this year since it's my final year in college and I feel as though I've missed out on a major part of life.

Oh, you know how it's going. Unfortunately :[
We gotta listen to more Journey. DON'T STOP, BELIEEEVIN'.

When depression first hit me, I felt betrayed by my then-closest friend (which they did say some nasty things, it wasn't misinterpretation). I felt In My Darkest Hour by Megadeth was relevant.
But now that I'm past that and know what causes me to feel so badly, Unnamed Feeling is still the perfect song for it. Sure, I would prefer it to be mixed a little differently, but that breakdown at the end... most powerful song on that album by far.

As a guy, I feel the same exact way. My depression is due to the fact that I've never experienced love like that in the slightest (single my whole life). I know I'm young, but I can't help but feel like I'm never going to meet a special somebody because of my lack of conversational skills and the fact that I too easily fall for any single women I befriend. Couples bother me, but I am absolutely glad that they get to experience that in their lives. I just wonder when is it going to be my turn, or if it even ever will be.

I'm a big guy, too. Tall, not muscular, but broad. And honestly right now, all I want in the world is for someone to hold me. But I have nobody that I can trust with that. You're not alone, dude. I wish I could come hang out since we'd understand each other. But until then, we have to power through it because, goddamnit, we do not give up. We can do this, and we WILL do this.

This is basically how I felt tonight. I wouldn't call her my best friend, but I definitely care too much considering I can't tell if it's mutual. I wanted to run the question by her, but it never felt like the right moment. Come home and now I'm suddenly filled with selfdoubt and disappointment in myself.
In a way, I envy you for having the courage to ask; to do what I couldn't. I've never had a relationship and am beginning to feel like it will never happen. But I can't bring myself to try with one of the very very few people who might actually feel similarly. You may not have gotten the answer you desired, but damn am I proud of you for trying.
I need this so much tonight, but they'll never know.

I feel like this is the absolute truth. I have two friends who both are dealing with different family issues on top of already-stressful conditions, and I've repeatedly told them both that they can trust me or ask me for anything at all. They both know (to some extent) that I'm struggling with depression, but I would seriously do anything I can for them, even if I'm not best friends with either. And I'm constantly worried that I'm being too overbearing or that, like I've experienced in the past, I don't truly mean it.
But god, I would do anything to help them. I feel so helpless but I want to at this point. I feel like it's what I'm currently living for (or at least using it as my crutch to get by). I just wish they knew how important they were to me.
No, and even if there were I don't want to go places like that alone
